chapter_seo_title: Desolate Era Ch. 454: The Endless Cupping Furnace Opens and Nine Hundred Fiendgods Are Freed
chapter_meta_description: Ji Ning's patience pays off as the bronze pillar triggers the release of over nine hundred imprisoned Void-level Fiendgods, shifting the balance of power against the Shaoyin clan.
og_title: The Prison Breaks Open! Ji Ning Sets an Army of Fiendgods Free
og_description: After a tense standoff, the Endless Cupping Furnace finally opens, releasing a horde of furious ancient Fiendgods who swear vengeance against the Shaoyin clan.
twitter_title: The perfect prison break. Ji Ning just unleashed an army of nine hundred Fiendgods on the Shaoyin clan.
twitter_description: Nine hundred ancient Fiendgods are freed from their prison, and they all owe a debt to Ji Ning.

surfaces: Eight Immortals Towning the Sea Formation
lore_anchors.definition: A high-level defensive formation requiring eight cultivators, named after the Eight Immortals of Chinese folklore. It acts as a powerful, coordinated defensive barrier or siege array.

The pinnacle stage of Fiendgod Body Refining before breaking through to become an Empyrean God. Each one possesses immense physical power and divine abilities, comparable to a veteran Celestial Immortal.
The ancient artifact buried beneath the Shaoyin clan's ancestral domain, identified by a distant, horned figure as his own. It served as a prison for hundreds of Fiendgods.

A failed Celestial Immortal who survived the Tribulation but could not ascend. They are powerful but bound by periodic, increasingly deadly tribulations, making them a more expendable asset than true Celestial Immortals in clan politics.

The highest grade of magic treasure within the Three Realms, ranked above Immortal treasures. A top-grade Pure Yang treasure is a priceless strategic asset, even for a being as ancient as the Shaoyin Patriarch.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the Endless Cupping Furnace?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It is an ancient artifact buried beneath the Shaoyin clan's domain that served as a prison for hundreds of Fiendgods. Ji Ning’s actions caused it to open and release them.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does the Shaoyin Patriarch refuse to sacrifice any Celestial Immortals?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Because Celestial Immortals are the true, irreplaceable foundation of a clan’s power. Sacrificing them would demoralize the leadership and destabilize the clan, whereas Loose Immortals and Earth Immortals are viewed as more expendable assets.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Who is the nine-headed Fiendgod leading the released prisoners?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He is the self-proclaimed leader of the "Furnace Tribe," a group of Fiendgods imprisoned and tortured by the Shaoyin clan. He declares a solemn oath to annihilate the Shaoyin clan for their suffering.
